text: Given a user has a registered MFA method and its method_id is known, When graph_delete_auth_method is called with user_id/method_type/method_id, Then Graph returns 204 and the tool reports deleted: true with the echoed params.

Given the method_id no longer exists for that user, When graph_delete_auth_method is called, Then Graph returns 404 and the tool still reports deleted: true (idempotent, same convention as graph_remove_managed_device/graph_remove_manager).
Given Graph returns a non-404 error (e.g. 500), When graph_delete_auth_method is called, Then the tool returns the standard error envelope and does not report deleted: true.
Given method_type is not one of the six supported values, When graph_delete_auth_method is called, Then the MCP schema rejects the call before any Graph request is made.

Given the tenant has not re-consented for UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All, When graph_delete_auth_method is called, Then Graph returns 403 and the tool returns the standard unauthorized envelope.

Given a real tenant and a real registered MFA method, When graph_list_auth_methods -> graph_delete_auth_method -> graph_list_auth_methods is run end to end on an INT test user, Then the targeted method is gone afterwards and no other tenant's data is touched or returned.
steps: On an INT test tenant, pick a test user with at least one registered MFA method
Call graph_list_auth_methods(user_id) and record a method_id + its method_type
expect: Second graph_list_auth_methods call no longer lists the deleted method_id; the call only affected the targeted tenant/user, no cross-tenant data appears in any response
notes: needs a real vendor account (two real tenants + a real registered MFA method); not a delivery blocker per the MCP track's no-test-account rule

text: Given a missing or invalid X-Ms-Graph-Token header, When graph_delete_auth_method is called, Then it returns the connector's standard not_configured/401 envelope, same as every other tool.
